description: How should domain objects obtain their dependencies and create their subordinates?
question: What is your default approach for object instantiation and dependency management?

options.name: Constructor Injection
options.description: Objects receive all dependencies through their constructor at creation time. Dependencies are explicit and immutable.
options.when_to_use: Dependencies are known at creation, immutability preferred, clear dependency graph, testability important
options.example: Order: Instantiated with: Customer, ShippingAddress, PaymentMethod

options.name: Self-Creating Objects
options.description: Objects know how to create themselves from context. Creation logic lives in the object being created, not external factory.
options.when_to_use: Domain logic determines creation, multiple creation paths, object owns its invariants
options.example: Order: Creates from shopping cart: Cart, Customer. Creates from quote: Quote, Customer

options.name: Factory Assembly
options.description: Dedicated factory objects assemble complex object graphs. Factory knows how to wire dependencies together.
options.when_to_use: Complex object graphs, many dependencies, assembly logic is reusable, framework integration
options.example: OrderFactory: Assembles order with: Cart, CustomerService, InventoryService, PaymentGateway

options.name: Container/Framework Managed
options.description: Dependency injection container or framework handles object creation and wiring. Configuration-driven.
options.when_to_use: Enterprise frameworks, cross-cutting concerns, infrastructure integration, team familiarity
options.example: Spring/Unity/Autofac container manages Order, injects CustomerRepository, PaymentGateway

options.name: Lazy Resolution
options.description: Dependencies resolved when first needed, not at construction. May use service locator or lazy injection.
options.when_to_use: Expensive dependencies, optional dependencies, circular dependency resolution
options.example: Portfolio: Get holdings resolves HoldingsRepository on first access
